prompt: The table below shows the percentage of adults who regularly bought goods online in six countries in 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020.

visuals.title: Adults who regularly shop online (% of adult population)

model:
The table compares the proportion of adults who regularly made purchases online in six countries at five-year intervals between 2005 and 2020.

Overall, online shopping became increasingly popular in every country listed. South Korea had the highest figure throughout, while Italy and Brazil, which started from a very low base, recorded the fastest relative growth.

In 2005, around a fifth of adults in South Korea (25%), the UK (22%), Japan (20%) and Germany (18%) shopped online, compared with only 4% in Italy and 3% in Brazil. Over the next fifteen years, the figure in South Korea more than tripled, reaching 88% in 2020, and the UK followed a similar pattern, rising to 83%. Germany also saw strong growth, to 76%, whereas the increase in Japan was more modest, with just under two thirds of adults (64%) buying goods online by the end of the period.

The two countries with the lowest initial rates experienced remarkable change. In Brazil, the proportion rose to 11% in 2010, overtaking Italy, and then climbed to 52% in 2020. Italy's figure grew more slowly at first but reached 49% by 2020, still the lowest in the table but roughly twelve times its 2005 level.
